description:
Make `Event` hold `id` and `timestamp` once around a tagged body, while serialized event-log lines keep their bytes.

## Background

Each event variant repeats `id` and `timestamp` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:1292-1616`). Draft constructors (`types.rs:1689-1980`) build variants with an empty id and an epoch timestamp, and the mutation finalizer stamps both through `assign_identity` (`types.rs:1653`, called at `repository_state/mutation.rs:1217`), with `sentinel_time` at `mutation.rs:495-500`. The canonical writer `serialize_event` (`mutation.rs:571-601`) sorts keys, so field order inside the struct does not reach the log. `parse_known_events` (`domain/event_log.rs:42`) decodes through `serde_json::Value`. Every matcher outside `domain/types.rs` already goes through `Event::body()`, a temporary `EventBody` alias and the identity accessors, and every construction outside it goes through draft constructors or the `test_utils` stamping helper.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Event` is a struct with `id`, `timestamp` and a flattened `body: EventBody`, and `EventBody` is the internally tagged enum whose variants carry neither id nor timestamp.
- [hard] REQ-02: Draft constructors return `EventBody`. In production only the mutation finalizer, event decoding and `EventTag::sample` (`domain/event_catalog.rs:280`, used by the generated reference and the events command) build an `Event`; `assign_identity`, the epoch sentinel and the `EventBody` alias no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each line of this repository's event log whose tag is a current event type decodes through the unchanged `parse_known_events` and re-serializes through the canonical writer to identical bytes, and the lines `parse_known_events` skips are exactly the lines carrying the retired tags `document_archived` and `lifecycle_timestamps_backfilled`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The published event schema still pins each variant's `type`, and the event catalog conformance tests pass.

## Notes

Raw `serde_json::to_string` key order changes from `type,id,...` to `id,timestamp,type,...`; this affects only the event command's stdout, which is not a stored shape.
title: Event becomes an envelope around a tagged body
